title: The Dog, the Cock, and the Fox
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Dog and a Cock became great friends, and agreed to travel together. At nightfall the Cock flew up into the branches of a tree to roost, while the Dog curled himself up inside the trunk, which was hollow. At break of day the Cock woke up and crew, as usual.

A Fox heard, and, wishing to make a breakfast of him, came and stood under the tree and begged him to come down. "I should so like," said he, "to make the acquaintance of one who has such a beautiful voice." The Cock replied, "Would you just wake my porter who sleeps at the foot of the tree? He'll open the door and let you in." The Fox accordingly rapped on the trunk, when out rushed the Dog and tore him in pieces.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what do the Dog and Cock agree to do?
options: Build a shared home
Guard a farmer's field
Travel together
Compete in a race

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where does the Cock roost at nightfall?
options: In the branches of a tree
Inside the hollow trunk with the Dog
On top of a nearby rock
Beside a running stream

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where does the Dog sleep for the night?
options: Beneath the lowest branches
Outside, guarding the base of the tree
In a den some distance away
Curled up inside the hollow trunk

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why does the Fox come and stand under the tree?
options: He wants to warn the Cock of danger
He wishes to make a breakfast of the Cock
He is looking for a place to rest
He is chasing another animal past the tree

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what excuse does the Fox give for wanting the Cock to come down?
options: To share breakfast together as new friends
To help him find his way through the forest
To make the acquaintance of one who has such a beautiful voice
To settle a dispute with another fox

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Cock tell the Fox to do first?
options: Wake his porter who sleeps at the foot of the tree
Climb the tree himself to greet him
Wait quietly until the Dog wakes on his own
Bring him some food as a gift first

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happens when the Fox raps on the trunk?
options: The Cock flies down to greet him
The trunk splits open and the Dog escapes
Nothing happens, since the Dog was not really inside
The Dog rushes out and tears him in pieces

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Cock call the Dog his "porter"?
options: He genuinely believes the Dog serves as a doorkeeper
He is playing along with the Fox's disguise while secretly setting a trap
He wants to distract the Fox from noticing the Dog at all
He is confused about which animal is inside the tree

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "roost" mean in "flew up into the branches of a tree to roost"?
options: To search for food at night
To build a nest for eggs
To settle somewhere to rest or sleep
To call out loudly before sunset

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: A clever partner can turn a predator's own trick back against him
Foxes should never approach a tree without checking it first
Dogs and roosters make poor traveling companions
Flattery always succeeds no matter who is targeted by it

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Cock do at break of day, as usual?
options: He flies down to find food
He wakes the Dog first
He waits silently for the Fox
He wakes up and crows

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Fox say he would like about the Cock?
options: That he is unusually large for a bird
That he has such a beautiful voice
That he travels with such a loyal companion
That he wakes so early every morning

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Cock claim the porter will do for the Fox?
options: Bring him something to eat
Carry a message to the Cock
Open the door and let him in
Guide him around to the front

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Fox's flattering request end up being fatal for him?
options: It leads him to knock on the very spot where the Dog is hidden
It causes the Cock to fly down within his reach
It wakes up other foxes nearby who chase him off
It draws the attention of the tree's actual owner

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Cock's calm reply to the Fox reveal about his state of mind?
options: He is genuinely flattered and eager to meet the Fox
He is frightened and stalling desperately for time
He does not realize the Fox intends him any harm
He is not fooled by the flattery and is already thinking a step ahead

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "acquaintance" mean in "to make the acquaintance of one who has such a beautiful voice"?
options: A gift exchanged between strangers
A person one has come to know
A song performed at a gathering
A formal written introduction

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Fox and a Cock become traveling companions after a chance meeting
A Dog abandons the Cock after the Fox approaches
A Fox tries to lure a Cock down with flattery but is instead caught by the Cock's hidden companion
A Cock is caught and eaten by the Fox at the base of the tree
